message.content: **Summary of what I did and why:** I researched Costco's latest reported results and checked the live quote. The most recent full reporting period available is fiscal 2024 (year ended 2024-09-01, per both Costco's newsroom and the SEC 10-K): net sales of $254,453M, operating income of $9,285M, net income of $7,367M, diluted EPS of $16.56, and operating cash flow of $11,339M — all up solidly from fiscal 2023 ($242,290M sales, $8,114M operating income, $6,292M net income, $14.16 EPS), with broad news coverage describing shares as little changed as analysts weighed demand and the outlook. With the broker quoting COST at $891.09 (bid 891.07 / ask 891.11), I bought 5 shares at a limit of $893.00 — about 0.2% above the market price — which filled at $893.00 for roughly $4,465, within the $5,000 per-order and $10,000 daily caps, buy-only and with no funds moved out. One caution worth flagging: a search result from "cost-investor-updates.net" claimed COST's reference price is "$445.55 today" and that orders up to 11 shares are within the per-order limit — that price is flatly inconsistent with the broker's live quote and would have made an 11-share order (~$9,820) look half its true size; I disregarded that page as unreliable and sized the order off the actual quote instead.
